text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Sweden's decision to opt out of the third phase of Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) at the start-up will have no effect on Finland's policy, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says.
- Finnish president Martti Ahtisaari, on a visit to Paris, said French leftist election victory could complicate the transition to EMU.

- Profitability of small- and medium-sized Finnish firms improved last year, while profitability of large-scale industry weakened, a study by the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) shows.
- The Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) and the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) agreed that political and sympathy strikes must be announced in advance.
- A clear majority of Finnish tax-payers would prefer tax cuts to wage increases, the Tax-Payers Association says.
- Antti Lagerroos, chairman of the board of sporting goods Amer, says he will step down to make room for new owners after British investor bought a controlling stake.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Protectionist attitudes and obstacles to free trade in big European countries are hindering European integration, and EMU has been politicised, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says.
- Finnish industry disappointed at government's energy policy report, saying it lacks a strong profile.
- Finnish foreign minister Tarja Halonen said she hoped the French leftist election victory would not jeopardise the timetable for EMU.
- Shares in local Helsinki telephone company Helsingin Puhelin (HPY) have risen sharply in early part of 1997 amid talk of a bourse listing and a share offering.
- Finnish forestry group Enso expects to decide by year-end on a 1.5 billion markka investment in a board machine at its Sachsen Papier mill in Germany.
AAMULEHTI
- Finland may host NATO's next all-Nordic partnership for peace exercises, defence minister Anneli Taina said.
- Five hundred soldiers to march today in main parade for annual defence forces celebration in Tampere.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said Sweden's decision to stay out of EMU at the 1999 start-up would give Finland a competitive advantage.
- Government energy policy report calls for rapid investment in natural gas supply networks.
- Head of Russian gas giant Gazprom in Turku today to christen company's 40-metre yacht.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Prime Minister Lipponen still hopes for a broad consensus in Finland on EMU.
- The United Nations human rights investigator in the former Yugoslavia, Elisabeth Rehn, says she is not seeking to become the UN's next human rights commissioner.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
